{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Deerskin / HDI Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2 — verified findings and recommended positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement on behalf of the Company (Customer). The document is unusually thin on risk-allocation architecture: it contains **no indemnification provision, no limitation of liability, no performance warranty, no IP/ownership allocation, no insurance covenant and no post-termination transition or data-return mechanic**. HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site, holds a licence to our Marks, and holds our Content and customer/user data on its own server, so these gaps sit squarely against us.

Three issues are the commercial priorities:

1. **No HDI IP-infringement indemnity (critical, missing).** Section 9 (Warranties) runs straight into Section 10 (General Provisions); the only third-party IP reference (Section 7.2) is a mutual advertising covenant. We have inserted a preferred-level HDI indemnity with claim procedure, plus a narrow Company indemnity limited to Company-provided Content and our own breach of law. We deliberately did **not** add a super-cap, which would only benefit HDI in an agreement with no liability cap.
2. **Exclusivity and non-compete on the Company (high).** Section 6.1 bars us from any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or "substantially similar" products for the full auto-renewing term, and hands HDI the exclusive right to use our own "Deerskin" brand for direct-to-consumer web sales. There is no automatic performance-based exit (Section 1.6 is a discretionary 70-day right only) and the sole carve-out (Section 6.2, closeout merchandise) is too narrow. We take the preferred position and replace the covenant with a no-exclusivity statement; HDI's reciprocal restriction in Section 6.3 benefits us and stays.
3. **Exit economics (high).** The Section 4.2 Termination Payment — half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly instalments — is uncapped and can far exceed three months' fees (fees are 30% of Net Sales under Section 3.1). We cap it at three months' Section 3 amounts and confirm it is the sole liquidated amount we owe, and we restate the Company's convenience right as a standalone sentence (it currently sits inside the auto-renewal sentence in Section 4.1) while limiting HDI's termination to the end of the then-current term.

Three rules are **compliant at the preferred position** and require no redline: no Customer MFN (Section 1.8's "no less favorably" covenant runs in our favour), no minimum purchase or volume commitment (pure revenue share above an $11,000 monthly floor), and no non-solicitation binding the Company.

Remaining medium and low items — audit frequency, dispute forum, licence scope for affiliates, renewal notice window, warranty, transition/data return, insurance, IP and liability cap — are addressed at the fallback level with the shortest workable edits, as noted in the table below.

---

## 2. Findings

| Sev. | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 (as marked) | Insert HDI indemnity (IP, breach of law, HDI-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice, control and cooperation procedure; narrow Company indemnity for Company-provided Content and our breach of law. No super-cap volunteered. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 (as marked); Section 10.3 | Section 10.3 is successors-and-assigns only and does not restrict HDI. Add one mutual provision: successor assignment on written notice; consent not unreasonably withheld for other assignments (fallback). |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 (as marked); Sections 6.1–6.3, 4.1, 1.6 | Full-term exclusive dealing with no automatic performance-based exit — walk-away territory. Replace the Company covenant and HDI's exclusive "Deerskin" brand right with a no-exclusivity statement (preferred); Section 6.3 retained. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 (as marked); Sections 6.1, 6.2, 4.1 | Open-ended "substantially similar products" scope, no internal-development or acquisition carve-out, not capped at 12 months due to annual auto-renewal. Remove the Company covenant and HDI's exclusive brand right (preferred); Sections 6.2 and 6.3 untouched. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation *(verification: repaired)* | § 1.4 (as marked); Sections 4.1, 4.2, 3.1 | Standalone Company convenience right on 90 days' notice (fallback); limit HDI's termination to the end of the then-current term; cap the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3 amounts. Preferred 30-day notice and pro-rata refund not pressed. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (as marked); Section 3.4 | Notice (30 days) and cost allocation already at or above fallback; no frequency limit. Single edit: cap inspections at once per year. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 5.4 (as marked); Section 10.5 | New York law matches preferred; no forum provision anywhere. Add one exclusive New York County forum sentence with temporary injunctive relief carve-out; choice-of-law wording untouched. |
| Medium | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (as marked); Sections 4.1, 4.2 | Uncapped stipulated exit amount. Add a proviso capping the Termination Payment at fees payable for the three months preceding the Termination Date and confirming it is the sole liquidated amount or penalty. Section 4.2(b) zero-floor preserved (favourable). |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 (as marked); Sections 1.4, 10.3 | Grant runs to "the Company" only (preamble definition excludes affiliates). Successor transfer already satisfied by Section 10.3. Single fallback edit: extend access/use rights to Company affiliates on written notice. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | **Compliant (preferred)** | § 1.4 (as marked); Sections 1.8, 3.1 | No Customer MFN; the "no less favorably" covenant in Section 1.8 runs in our favour. No redline. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | **Compliant (preferred)** | § 1.4 (as marked); Sections 3.1, 1.2, 1.6, 1.8, 2.2 | Pure revenue share above an $11,000 monthly floor; no minimum spend, take-or-pay or volume cap. Section 4.2 exit fee reviewed under T4C/LD, not double-flagged. No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Compliant (preferred)** | § 5.4 (as marked) | No solicitation, hiring or no-hire restriction on the Company anywhere. Noted for the file: we likewise have no non-solicit protection against HDI, and the playbook does not require us to introduce one. No redline. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal / non-renewal notice | Deviation | § 1.4 (as marked); Section 4.1 | 90-day non-renewal window exceeds the 60-day fallback maximum. Shorten the Company's notice to 60 days; keep HDI's 90-day notice and the 12-month renewal term. No renewal uplift mechanic, so the price-cap element is not engaged. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 (as marked); Sections 4, 1.4/1.5, 8 | No effects-of-termination, transition, export or deletion mechanic; access and export files exist only during the term. Insert fallback clause: at least 90 days' transition assistance and data export within 30 days of expiry or termination. Preferred six-month/certified-deletion package not pressed. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.4 (as marked); Section 9 | Section 9 is corporate authority plus the Globix acknowledgement only; no performance warranty or remedy. Insert fallback warranty: 90-day documentation conformance for the Site and HDI software, 30-day services conformance, repair/replacement or refund at the Company's election. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 (as marked); Sections 10.1–10.8 | No insurance covenant despite HDI hosting the Site and processing our user and order data. Insert fallback clause: E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber and privacy USD 2,000,000. CGL, workers' compensation and certificate mechanics not pursued. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 5.4 (as marked); Section 6.1 | No IP allocation; only a narrow Marks licence. Insert Section 5.5 at fallback: HDI retains generic tools and know-how; Company receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Site and deliverables; HDI's licence in Company data limited to providing the Services. Preferred assignment of the Site not pushed given HDI bears development costs under Section 1.2. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 (as marked); Sections 1–10, 10.2 | No cap, exclusive remedy or consequential-damages exclusion; both parties uncapped. Insert new Section 10.9 at fallback: mutual cap at fees paid or payable by the Company in the preceding 12 months, with confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence and wilful misconduct uncapped. Preferred floor and additional carve-outs held in reserve. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points our findings place in walk-away territory. We should not sign without movement on them.

1. **Absence of an HDI IP-infringement indemnity (INDEMN, critical).** HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and licenses our Marks; the total absence of an IP indemnity is walk-away territory under the rule. There is also no limitation of liability to soften it.
2. **Section 6.1 exclusivity (EXCLUSIVITY, high).** Exclusive dealing for the full auto-renewing term with no automatic performance-based exit is walk-away territory. HDI's exclusive hold on our own "Deerskin" brand for direct-to-consumer web sales compounds this.
3. **Absence of any insurance covenant (INSURANCE, low severity but flagged).** For a vendor that processes our Content, user information and customer order data, the absence of coverage sits in walk-away territory under the rule.

Near the line, and worth watching in negotiation:

- **Section 3.4 audit with no frequency limit** — edges toward walk-away territory; the once-per-year cap is a minimal ask.
- **90-day non-renewal notice window** — at the edge of walk-away territory under the renewal rule.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** reflecting the proposals above: the HDI indemnity, the no-exclusivity replacement for Section 6.1, the Termination Payment cap and standalone convenience right, the IP section, the mutual liability cap, the warranty, the transition/data-export clause, the insurance covenant and the exclusive New York forum sentence, plus the short edits to Sections 1.4 (affiliates), 3.4 (once per year), 4.1 (60-day Company notice) and 10.3 (mutual assignment).
2. **Lead with the three walk-away items** in the first negotiation session — indemnity, Section 6.1 exclusivity, and insurance — and treat the remaining fallback-level edits as a package to be closed together.
3. **Confirm the exit maths with the business team**: quantify the Section 4.2 formula (half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000) against expected Net Sales so we can show HDI the exposure the three-month cap is addressing.
4. **Hold in reserve** the preferred positions we have not pressed (30-day convenience notice and pro-rata refund; 12-month software warranty and no-malicious-code; six-month transition with certified deletion; USD 1,000,000 liability floor and the wider carve-out set; assignment of the Site) for use if HDI resists the fallback package.
5. **Note for the file**: the T4C finding is marked as verification "repaired"; we will re-check that clause's final wording against Sections 4.1, 4.2 and 3.1 before the redline goes out.
6. **Flag internally** that the Agreement contains no non-solicit protection running against HDI. This is compliant under our playbook and we are not proposing to introduce one, but the business should be aware.
"}
